# The sharp fixed-mass centroid-tail constant for a density sandwich

This note concerns precisely rho=1_B dx+2 eta, with 0<=eta<=1_B dx.
It does not assert that arbitrary optimized mixed capacities have this
form. In fact `candidate a26d4b26fb2a803f`
disproves the proposed universal capacity-mean OC budget.

Let d>=1, gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, q=1+1/d, and fix alpha in [0,1].
Consider all d-dimensional convex bodies B and submeasures eta with
eta(B)=alpha |B|. Let g be the centroid of rho. The sharp lower bound
for rho(H)/rho(B), over all closed halfspaces H containing g, is the
following explicitly attained two-scalar minimum:

 Theta_d(alpha)=min (s+2r)/(1+2alpha),                (1)

where the compact domain is

 0<=s<=1,
 0<=r<=min(alpha,s),
 s+alpha-r<=1,

 q(1+2alpha)s^(q-1)
       >=1+2r^q+2(s+alpha-r)^q-2s^q.               (2)

Every minimizing pair has 0<s<1 and equality in the last constraint.
Every such minimizing pair is realized by a uniform simplex with eta
equal to ordinary volume on two bands of parallel simplex sections.
Thus (1)-(2) are a complete exact finite characterization for this
density class, with no unproved extremal-body or existence assertion.

## 1. Necessity of the scalar constraints

Normalize |B|=1. It suffices to use a parallel halfspace whose boundary
passes through g. Since rho has density at least one on B, g is in its
interior, and the ordinary volume s of that cap lies in (0,1). Put
r=eta(H). The elementary domination constraints are exactly the first
three lines of (2).

For the scalar projection X in the cap direction, let U(t) be its
uniform-B upper-tail volume and G(t)=U(t)^(1/d). Brunn-Minkowski makes
G concave on its projection interval. The random variable U(X) is
uniform on [0,1] under uniform B; the pushforward of eta therefore has
a density h(v) between zero and one, with total alpha and mass r on
[0,s]. Jensen at the rho centroid gives

 (1+2alpha)s^(1/d)
      >=d/(d+1)+2 integral_0^1 v^(1/d)h(v)dv.        (3)

Among densities between zero and one of mass r on [0,s], the increasing
integrand is minimized by filling [0,r]. Among those of mass alpha-r
on [s,1], it is minimized by filling [s,s+alpha-r]. This elementary
bathtub argument follows by subtracting the leftmost-interval indicator
and then subtracting the integrand's cutoff value: both parts of the
resulting weighted integrand are nonnegative. Hence

 integral_0^1 v^(1/d)h(v)dv
 >=(1/q)[r^q+(s+alpha-r)^q-s^q].                    (4)

Substitution into (3) gives the last constraint of (2), while the
normalized rho cap mass is precisely (s+2r)/(1+2alpha).

## 2. Attainment and the exact extremizers

The feasible set in (2) is compact and nonempty: s=1,r=alpha belongs
to it. At this pair the last inequality is strict, because its
left-minus-right side is

 q(1+2alpha)-1-2alpha^q
    =(q-1)+2alpha(q-alpha^(1/d))>0.

At s=0 the domination constraints force r=0, and the last inequality
is false. Thus every feasible point has s>0, and compactness gives an
attained minimum in (1).

Suppose a minimizing pair had strict inequality in (2). If r>0,
decrease s and r by the same sufficiently small positive epsilon.
The constraints r<=s and s+alpha-r<=1 are unchanged, and the other
constraints persist. By continuity the last inequality remains true,
while the objective decreases by 3epsilon/(1+2alpha), a contradiction.
If r=0, decrease s alone by a small epsilon, obtaining the same
contradiction. Consequently the last constraint is an equality at
every minimizer. Since s=1 forces r=alpha and the inequality there is
strict, every minimizer has s<1 as well.

To realize a minimizing pair, take a simplex B of volume one and its
vertex barycentric coordinate X. Then

 U(t)=(1-t)^d,  0<=t<=1,
 X=1-U(X)^(1/d).

Let eta be ordinary volume restricted to the two quantile bands

 {U(X) in [0,r] union [s,s+alpha-r]}.                (5)

They overlap only on a null boundary, and eta has mass alpha. Its
projection moment is alpha minus the integral in (4), now with
equality. Since E_B X=1/(d+1), the projection of its rho centroid is

 X_g=1-[d/(d+1)+2 integral v^(1/d)h(v)dv]/(1+2alpha).

The equality case of (2) says exactly that X_g=1-s^(1/d). Therefore
the upper cap through the actual rho centroid has ordinary volume s
and eta mass r, and realizes (1). The remaining centroid coordinates
are immaterial: the cap is defined solely by X=X_g and passes through
the full centroid by definition. This proves equality between the
infinite-body infimum and the attained scalar minimum.

## 3. An explicit quantitative bound without scalar minimization

A one-interval version of the bathtub argument gives

 integral_0^1 v^(1/d)h(v)dv
       >=[d/(d+1)]alpha^(1+1/d).

Define

 L_d(alpha)=gamma_d
       [1+2alpha^(1+1/d)]^d/(1+2alpha)^d.            (6)

Equation (3) implies s>=L_d(alpha). Domination also gives
r>=max(0,s+alpha-1). Consequently every such law satisfies

 rho(H)/rho(B)
 >= max{L_d(alpha), 3L_d(alpha)+2alpha-2}/(1+2alpha).
                                                        (7)

One may additionally take the maximum of the right side with gamma_d/2,
by the already proved density-sandwich centroid inequality. In
particular the simpler bound

 rho(H)/rho(B)
 >=gamma_d[1+2alpha^(1+1/d)]^d/(1+2alpha)^(d+1)       (8)

gives an explicit deficit from gamma_d tending to zero as alpha tends
to zero. Formula (7) also returns gamma_d exactly at alpha=1, when
rho is just three times uniform volume. At alpha=0 it likewise returns
ordinary gamma_d. Indeed the exact constant satisfies
Theta_d(0)=Theta_d(1)=gamma_d, either from (2) or from uniform-simplex
sharpness.

These statements apply to the specific law 1_B+2 1_E in
`candidate d26e9d073c9268ac`, with
alpha=1/100. They do not supply a universal bound in terms of endpoint
imbalance: that example already has equal endpoint volumes and still
has a strict deficit below gamma_2. Nor does a density-class bound
repair the falsified capacity-slack rule for arbitrary optimized laws.
